# Start here: seven steps before Lab 1

All seven steps take about 45 minutes, plus any time your IT team needs. The Monday cohort starts September 28 and the Friday cohort on October 2. Tap Done as you finish each step.

**Short on time? Come anyway.** You can use Claude in your browser for the day, and a facilitator helps you finish setup.

1. **Your seat is confirmed**. Nothing to do here. Your organization confirmed your two seats, so this one is done already.
2. **Send your intake**. Each of you sends your own on the intake page, and sending it ticks this step for you. It takes about 14 minutes. The form ends with a checklist about your setup. Tick only what you've already done and send it, even if setup isn't finished. Monday cohort by Friday, September 25 · Friday cohort by Wednesday, September 30 · Late? Send it anyway.

3. **RSVP and test Zoom**. Use the RSVP link in Nichole Giller's welcome email to put your seven sessions, with the Zoom link, on your calendar. Then open Zoom on the computer you'll use and check that your sound works and you can share your screen. This takes about 5 minutes.

4. **Get Claude Pro and the desktop app**. This takes about 15 minutes, plus any time IT needs. If your organization already gives you a Claude seat, use that. Otherwise, sign up at [claude.ai](https://claude.ai) with your own email and choose Pro, monthly rather than annual. Each of you gets your own account, and it stays yours. Wells Fargo covers the cost for six months, and Rachel Bruce from RW Institute emails you about how the payment reaches you. **If you'd rather wait for that first payment before you enter a card, that's fine: come to Lab 1 anyway and use a free Claude account in your browser for the day. Sign up free at claude.ai (signing in with Google is quickest) and upgrade that same account to Pro when you're ready.** Then install the Claude desktop app from claude.ai/download and sign in. If IT won't allow the install, use Claude in your browser.

5. **Make one folder, then save three files into it**. This takes about 4 minutes. Make an empty folder called `AI-Labs`, spelled with the hyphen. Each of you makes your own, because you each write your own files in Lab 1. Use Documents, not the Desktop folder: in testing, Cowork couldn't open one on a Desktop synced to OneDrive. If it can't open the folder wherever you put it, use Claude in your browser for the lab. Then click each file below. It saves to your computer, usually in Downloads. Drag all three into `AI-Labs`. Files: The Lab 1 kit (lab-1.md) · The practice email thread · The interview prompt. You don't open or use any of them before the lab. The kit is the step-by-step for Lab 1. The practice email thread is a set of made-up emails from a fictional nonprofit, for anyone who doesn't bring writing of their own. The interview prompt is what Claude uses in Lab 1 to learn about your organization. Lab 1 needs only these three, plus the ship log if you use Claude in your browser. The Lab 1 card further down links to the same files.

6. **Paste two prompts into Cowork**. This takes about 4 minutes. Open Cowork, the part of the Claude desktop app that works on a folder on your computer, and choose `AI-Labs` as the folder Claude works in. Choose AI-Labs itself, not Documents or a folder inside it, so Claude works only in AI-Labs. Paste prompt 1, wait for Claude to finish, then paste prompt 2. If Claude asks for your OK before it changes anything, give it.

**Prompt 1**

Makes four folders in AI-Labs (Kits, Working, Recipes and Outputs) and your ship log.

```text
First check the folder I chose to work in. If it isn't called AI-Labs, don't change anything. Just tell me its name. If it is, make these four folders in it, unless they're already there: Kits, Working, Recipes and Outputs. Then, unless Outputs/ship-log.md already exists, make it with exactly these two lines:
# Ship log
One line for each thing you send with Claude's help: the date, what it was, who it went to (a group like "board" or "volunteers", never the name of a client, donor or volunteer), old way __ minutes, new way __ minutes, both timed on a stopwatch.
Don't move, open or change anything else. Then list everything in the folder so I can check it, and end your reply with this line on its own: AI-Labs is set up.
```

**You're done when:**

Claude’s last line says “AI-Labs is set up.”

**Prompt 2**

Writes TO-DO.md, your list for Lab 1, and moves the three files into Kits. A file ending in .md is plain text that Claude, and any other AI tool, can read and write.

```text
First check the folder I chose to work in. If it isn't called AI-Labs, don't change anything. Just tell me its name. If it is, make a file called TO-DO.md at the top of AI-Labs, unless it's already there, with exactly this text:

# To do
A markdown file (.md) is a plain text file that Claude, and any other AI tool, can read and write. This one is your to-do list. Ask Claude to tick things off as you go.

## Before Lab 1
- [ ] Send the intake
- [ ] RSVP with the link in Nichole's welcome email, and test Zoom screen sharing
- [ ] Claude Pro (monthly) and the desktop app
- [x] AI-Labs folder set up
- [ ] Lab 1 files in Kits
- [ ] Ready check says "Ready for Lab 1"
- [ ] Pick one small piece of writing to bring that names no client, donor or volunteer, or plan to use the practice thread

## In Lab 1
- [ ] Get interviewed, and Claude writes AGENTS.md
- [ ] Readback test
- [ ] One real item checked and ready to send
- [ ] Save the brief as a recipe and add a line to the ship log

Then move these files into Kits if they're anywhere in AI-Labs outside Kits: KIT-Lab1-First-Safe-Win.md, MOCK-Program-Update-Email-Thread.txt, STARTER-AGENTS.md, and STARTER-Ship-Log.md if it's there. Don't open or change them. If the first three are all in Kits, tick "Lab 1 files in Kits" in TO-DO.md, list everything in the folder, and end your reply with this line on its own: Your Lab 1 files and to-do list are ready. If any of the first three is missing, list the folder and end your reply with "Missing:" and the names of the missing files.
```

**You're done when:**

Claude’s last line says “Your Lab 1 files and to-do list are ready.” If it ends with “Missing:” instead, save the file it names into AI-Labs and paste prompt 2 again.

**Using Claude in your browser instead**

The prompts need Cowork. In the browser, including a free account, skip steps 6 and 7: in Lab 1, step 4 has you make a Project called `AI-Labs`, which takes the place of the folders. Tap Done on both.

7. **Run the ready check**. This takes a minute. In the same Cowork session, paste the ready check. It looks at your folder and changes nothing. In the browser, there's no ready check yet: tap Done, and you'll set up your Project in Lab 1, step 4.

**Ready check**

Looks at your AI-Labs folder and tells you whether anything is missing.

```text
Check my AI-Labs folder, and don't change anything. Look for these: the folders Kits, Working, Recipes and Outputs; the files TO-DO.md and Outputs/ship-log.md; and in Kits, KIT-Lab1-First-Safe-Win.md, MOCK-Program-Update-Email-Thread.txt and STARTER-AGENTS.md. Keep your reply short, and end it with exactly one of these lines. If the folder I chose isn't called AI-Labs: "Not yet: start a new Cowork session and choose the AI-Labs folder itself." If everything is there: "Ready for Lab 1." If anything is missing: "Not yet:" followed by the first missing item and the prompt that fixes it, prompt 1 for the folders and the ship log, prompt 2 for TO-DO.md and the Lab 1 files.
```

**You're done when:**

Claude’s last line says “Ready for Lab 1.” If it says “Not yet:”, paste the prompt it names, then check again.

**One more thing before Lab 1.** Each of you picks one small piece of writing that's due this week to bring, or uses the practice email thread; the steps are the same, and you each write your own in Lab 1. Clients, donors, volunteers and anyone you serve never go into Claude or your AI-Labs folder, and neither do health or case details. Staff names in your everyday writing are fine. If you run out of time for any of this, come anyway: you can use Claude in your browser for the day, and a facilitator helps you finish setup.

Stuck on a step? Email Nichole Giller at RW Institute, nichole@realizedworth.com, with the step's name and a screenshot.

This site records the steps you mark done, which pages and sections you read and roughly for how long, and your answers to the weekly questions, linked to the email you give us. The RW Institute team sees all of it. PCI sees counts only, never your name or anything you write. Nobody at RW Institute or PCI can see your Claude chats or files.
